# pylint: disable=protected-access

"""Finding the sign-in of an MCP server with its own (RFC 9728 and RFC 8414).

The MCP server names its authorization server, so what the gateway fetches,
and where it sends codes and client secrets, must stay https and its own.
"""

from unittest.mock import patch

import httpx
import pytest

from mcp_gateway.oauth import mcp_oauth_discovery as mod

ORIGIN = "https://mcp.example.com"
MCP_URL = f"{ORIGIN}/v1/mcp"
ORIGIN_OAUTH = f"{ORIGIN}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server"
ORIGIN_OIDC = f"{ORIGIN}/.well-known/openid-configuration"
ENDPOINTS = {
    "authorization_endpoint": "https://mcp.example.com/auth",
    "token_endpoint": "https://mcp.example.com/token",
}


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True, name="_fresh_cache")
def fixture_fresh_cache():
    mod.clear_discovery_cache()
    yield
    mod.clear_discovery_cache()


def _serve(documents):
    """Answer metadata fetches from ``documents``, keyed by URL; returns the URLs fetched."""
    fetched = []

    async def _fetch(url):
        fetched.append(url)
        document = documents.get(url)
        if isinstance(document, Exception):
            raise document
        return document

    return fetched, patch.object(mod, "_fetch_json", side_effect=_fetch)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "documents",
    [
        pytest.param({ORIGIN_OAUTH: ENDPOINTS}, id="the origin's oauth metadata"),
        pytest.param({ORIGIN_OIDC: ENDPOINTS}, id="the origin's openid configuration"),
        pytest.param(
            {
                ORIGIN_OAUTH: {"issuer": "https://mcp.example.com"},
                ORIGIN_OIDC: ENDPOINTS,
            },
            id="past a document without endpoints",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            {ORIGIN_OAUTH: httpx.ConnectError("refused"), ORIGIN_OIDC: ENDPOINTS},
            id="past an unreachable candidate",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            {
                f"{ORIGIN}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp": {
                    "authorization_servers": ["https://auth.example.com"]
                },
                "https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server": (
                    ENDPOINTS
                ),
            },
            id="the authorization server the resource names",
        ),
    ],
)
async def test_a_servers_endpoints_are_discovered(documents):
    _fetched, serving = _serve(documents)

    with serving:
        metadata = await mod.resolve_oauth_metadata(MCP_URL, None)

    assert metadata.token_endpoint == ENDPOINTS["token_endpoint"]


async def test_a_configured_metadata_url_is_the_only_one_fetched_and_is_cached():
    metadata_url = "https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server"
    fetched, serving = _serve({metadata_url: ENDPOINTS})

    with serving:
        await mod.resolve_oauth_metadata(MCP_URL, metadata_url)
        metadata = await mod.resolve_oauth_metadata(MCP_URL, metadata_url)

    assert metadata.token_endpoint == ENDPOINTS["token_endpoint"]
    assert fetched == [metadata_url]


async def test_an_unreachable_configured_metadata_url_is_an_error():
    _fetched, serving = _serve({})

    with serving, pytest.raises(ValueError, match="could not fetch"):
        await mod.resolve_oauth_metadata(MCP_URL, "https://auth.example.com/x")


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "mcp_url, document, refusal",
    [
        # A server's metadata must be its own (RFC 8414 section 3.3).
        pytest.param(
            MCP_URL,
            {**ENDPOINTS, "issuer": "https://other.example.com"},
            "issuer",
            id="another issuer",
        ),
        # Otherwise codes and client secrets would travel in the clear.
        pytest.param(
            MCP_URL,
            {**ENDPOINTS, "token_endpoint": "http://10.0.0.5/token"},
            "https",
            id="an http token endpoint",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            MCP_URL,
            {**ENDPOINTS, "registration_endpoint": "http://10.0.0.5/r"},
            "https",
            id="an http registration endpoint",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            "http://mcp.internal/mcp",
            {
                "authorization_endpoint": "http://mcp.internal/auth",
                "token_endpoint": "http://mcp.internal/token",
            },
            "https",
            id="an http server",
        ),
    ],
)
async def test_metadata_that_isnt_the_servers_own_or_https_is_refused(
    monkeypatch, mcp_url, document, refusal
):
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod.settings, "DEBUG", False)

    with (
        patch.object(mod, "_fetch_json", return_value=document),
        pytest.raises(ValueError, match=refusal),
    ):
        await mod.discover_oauth_metadata(mcp_url)


async def test_an_http_authorization_server_named_by_the_mcp_server_is_not_fetched(
    monkeypatch,
):
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod.settings, "DEBUG", False)
    fetched, serving = _serve(
        {
            f"{ORIGIN}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp": {
                "authorization_servers": ["http://169.254.169.254"]
            }
        }
    )

    with serving, pytest.raises(ValueError, match="https"):
        await mod.discover_oauth_metadata(MCP_URL)

    assert not any("169.254" in url for url in fetched)


async def test_a_client_secret_needs_a_configured_metadata_url():
    """The MCP server must not choose the token endpoint the secret goes to."""
    fetched, serving = _serve({})

    with serving, pytest.raises(ValueError, match="metadata URL"):
        await mod.resolve_oauth_metadata(MCP_URL, None, has_client_secret=True)

    assert not fetched


async def test_discovery_does_not_follow_redirects():
    """A redirect could send the gateway's request anywhere."""
    requests = []

    def handler(request):
        requests.append(request.url)
        return httpx.Response(302, headers={"Location": "http://169.254.169.254/"})

    transport = httpx.MockTransport(handler)
    real_client = httpx.AsyncClient

    def client(**kwargs):
        return real_client(transport=transport, **kwargs)

    with patch.object(mod.httpx, "AsyncClient", client):
        assert await mod._fetch_json("https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/x") is None

    assert [str(url) for url in requests] == ["https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/x"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "endpoint, scope",
    [
        ("https://slack.com/oauth", "chat:write,channels:read"),
        ("https://x/oauth", "chat:write channels:read"),
    ],
)
def test_only_slack_gets_comma_separated_scopes(endpoint, scope):
    assert mod.scope_param_for_authorize("chat:write channels:read", endpoint) == scope


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "response, parsed",
    [
        (
            {"access_token": "abc", "refresh_token": "r1", "expires_in": 300},
            ("abc", "r1", 300),
        ),
        # Slack's wrapper; without expires_in or a refresh token it lasts until revoked.
        (
            {"ok": True, "access_token": "xoxp"},
            ("xoxp", None, mod._NON_EXPIRING_TTL_SECONDS),
        ),
        (
            {"access_token": "abc", "refresh_token": "r1"},
            ("abc", "r1", mod._DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS),
        ),
    ],
    ids=["standard", "slack, until revoked", "refreshable, an hour"],
)
def test_a_token_response_gives_the_token_its_refresh_token_and_lifetime(
    response, parsed
):
    assert mod.parse_token_response(response) == parsed


def test_a_slack_error_response_is_an_error():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        mod.parse_token_response({"ok": False, "error": "invalid_code"})

"""How the gateway signs in to MCP servers for service accounts
(mcp_gateway.oauth.mcp_service_auth)."""

import base64
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock

import pytest

from mcp_gateway.config import settings
from mcp_gateway.models import MCPCatalog, ServiceAccountCredentials, User
from mcp_gateway.oauth import mcp_service_auth

SECRET_REF = "mcp-gateway-sa-trino-creds"


def _forwarding(**trino):
    return {"downstream_credentials": {"trino": trino}}


@pytest.fixture(name="storage")
def fixture_storage(monkeypatch):
    """The secret store, holding the service account's credential."""
    storage = MagicMock()
    storage.get_secret = [REDACTED]"secret-pass")
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_service_auth, "get_secret_storage", lambda: storage)
    return storage


@pytest.fixture(name="forward")
def fixture_forward(db_session, service_account, storage):
    """The headers the service account forwards to trino, given its config."""

    async def _forward(additional_config):
        db_session.add(
            ServiceAccountCredentials(
                service_account_id=service_account.id,
                provider="google",
                service_account_name="svc-test@example.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
                allowed_services=["trino"],
                created_by=service_account.id,
                additional_config=additional_config,
            )
        )
        db_session.commit()
        return await mcp_service_auth.build_credential_forward_headers(
            db_session, service_account, "trino"
        )

    return _forward


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "is_service_account, service_auth_type, expected",
    [
        (True, "credential_forward", "credential_forward"),
        (True, "", "oauth"),
        (False, "credential_forward", "oauth"),
    ],
)
def test_a_service_account_uses_the_servers_service_auth_type_when_set(
    is_service_account, service_auth_type, expected
):
    mcp = MCPCatalog(auth_type="oauth", service_auth_type=service_auth_type)
    user = User(is_service_account=is_service_account)

    assert mcp_service_auth.effective_auth_type(mcp, user) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "trino, header",
    [
        (
            {"secret_ref": SECRET_REF, "auth_header_type": "basic", "username": "u1"},
            "Basic " + base64.b64encode(b"u1:secret-pass").decode(),
        ),
        (
            {"secret_ref": SECRET_REF, "auth_header_type": "bearer"},
            "Bearer secret-pass",
        ),
    ],
)
async def test_the_secret_is_forwarded_in_the_configured_header(
    forward, storage, trino, header
):
    headers = await forward(_forwarding(**trino))

    assert headers == {"Authorization": header}
    storage.get_secret.assert_awaited_once_with(SECRET_REF)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "config",
    [
        {},
        _forwarding(secret_ref=SECRET_REF),
        _forwarding(secret_ref=SECRET_REF, auth_header_type="digest"),
        _forwarding(secret_ref=SECRET_REF, auth_header_type="basic"),
        _forwarding(auth_header_type="bearer"),
    ],
    ids=["none", "no-header-type", "unknown-header-type", "no-username", "no-secret"],
)
async def test_an_incomplete_forwarding_config_forwards_nothing(
    forward, storage, config
):
    assert await forward(config) is None
    storage.get_secret.assert_not_awaited()


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "secret_ref",
    [
        "mcp-gateway-encryption-key",
        "arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-west-2:123456789012:secret:prod-db",
        "projects/other/secrets/db-password",
        "unrelated-secret",
    ],
)
async def test_only_service_account_secrets_are_forwarded(forward, storage, secret_ref):
    """The gateway can read other secrets, its own encryption key among them."""
    headers = await forward(
        _forwarding(secret_ref=secret_ref, auth_header_type="bearer")
    )

    assert headers is None
    storage.get_secret.assert_not_awaited()


def test_the_encryption_key_is_refused_even_without_a_prefix(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SECRET_PREFIX", "")

    assert mcp_service_auth.refused_secret_refs(
        _forwarding(secret_ref="mcp-gateway-encryption-key")
    ) == ["mcp-gateway-encryption-key"]
    assert not mcp_service_auth.refused_secret_refs(_forwarding(secret_ref="any-name"))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("config", [None, {}, {"downstream_credentials": "junk"}])
def test_configs_without_forwarding_refuse_nothing(config):
    assert not mcp_service_auth.refused_secret_refs(config)

"""Connecting a person to an MCP server, and disconnecting them.

Servers with single sign-on get the person's token from the gateway's identity
provider; servers with their own sign-in, from theirs. Someone can start
connecting, then send another person the link the provider redirects to, so a
callback stores a token only for the person who started, in their own browser.
"""

import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, patch
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit

import httpx
import jwt
import pytest
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

from mcp_gateway.config import settings
from mcp_gateway.models import MCPCatalog, OAuthState, OAuthToken
from mcp_gateway.oauth.mcp_oauth_discovery import OAuthServerMetadata
from mcp_gateway.oauth.token_encryption import TokenEncryption
from mcp_gateway.routes import mcp_oauth
from mcp_gateway.routes.mcp_oauth import _resolve_client_id
from mcp_gateway.sessions import SESSION_TYPE, session_cookie_name

REDIRECT_URI = "https://mcp-gateway.example.com/callback"


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True, name="_encryption")
def fixture_encryption(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "mcp_gateway.oauth.token_manager.get_token_encryption",
        AsyncMock(return_value=TokenEncryption(b"k" * 32)),
    )


def _sign_in(client, user_id):
    token = jwt.encode(
        {"user_id": user_id, "type": SESSION_TYPE},
        settings.JWT_SECRET_KEY,
        algorithm=settings.JWT_ALGORITHM,
    )
    client.cookies.set(session_cookie_name(), token)


def _catalog(db, **extra):
    """A server with its own sign-in, unless ``extra`` says otherwise."""
    row = MCPCatalog(
        **{
            "service_id": "docs",
            "name": "Docs",
            "mcp_url": "https://docs.example.com/mcp",
            "auth_type": "oauth",
            "auto_sso_enabled": False,
            "is_active": True,
            **extra,
        }
    )
    db.add(row)
    db.commit()
    return row


def _tokens(db, service):
    return db.query(OAuthToken).filter(OAuthToken.service == service).all()


@pytest.fixture(name="dcr_metadata")
def fixture_dcr_metadata() -> OAuthServerMetadata:
    return OAuthServerMetadata(
        authorization_endpoint="https://auth.example.com/authorize",
        token_endpoint="https://auth.example.com/token",
        registration_endpoint="https://auth.example.com/register",
    )


@pytest.fixture(name="discovered")
def fixture_discovered(monkeypatch, dcr_metadata):
    """The server's authorization server, found without network calls."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "mcp_gateway.routes.mcp_oauth.resolve_oauth_metadata",
        AsyncMock(return_value=dcr_metadata),
    )


@pytest.fixture(name="register")
def fixture_register(monkeypatch):
    """Dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) at the authorization server."""
    register = AsyncMock(return_value="dcr-issued-cid")
    monkeypatch.setattr("mcp_gateway.routes.mcp_oauth.register_oauth_client", register)
    return register


# --- starting to connect ---------------------------------------------------------


def test_a_server_with_its_own_sign_in_is_connected_through_its_discovery(
    client, db_session, regular_user
):
    _catalog(db_session)
    _sign_in(client, regular_user.id)

    resp = client.get("/portal/connect/docs", follow_redirects=False)

    assert resp.status_code in (302, 307)
    assert resp.headers["location"].endswith("/portal/connect-mcp-oauth/docs")


def test_connecting_an_unknown_service_returns_404(client, regular_user):
    _sign_in(client, regular_user.id)

    resp = client.get("/portal/connect/nosuchservice", follow_redirects=False)

    assert resp.status_code == 404
    assert resp.json()["detail"] == "Service 'nosuchservice' not found"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "path", ["/portal/connect/docs", "/portal/connect-mcp-oauth/docs"]
)
def test_a_person_who_is_not_an_admin_cannot_connect_to_an_admin_only_server(
    client, db_session, regular_user, path
):
    """Starting the sign-in would register a client and store a token."""
    _catalog(db_session, oauth_client_id="docs-client", admin_only=True)
    _sign_in(client, regular_user.id)

    resp = client.get(path, follow_redirects=False)

    assert resp.status_code == 404


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "provider, server, scope",
    [
        (
            "keycloak",
            {"audience": "gravitino", "oauth_scopes": "gravitino:read"},
            "openid profile email offline_access gravitino:read",
        ),
        # Entra issues a token for one app at a time, so the gateway asks for the server's.
        (
            "azure",
            {"audience": "gravitino-app-id"},
            "api://gravitino-app-id/.default offline_access",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_connecting_with_single_sign_on_asks_for_the_servers_scopes(
    client, db_session, regular_user, monkeypatch, provider, server, scope
):
    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "OIDC_PROVIDER", provider)
    _catalog(db_session, service_id="gravitino", auto_sso_enabled=True, **server)
    _sign_in(client, regular_user.id)

    resp = client.get("/portal/connect/gravitino", follow_redirects=False)

    assert parse_qs(urlsplit(resp.headers["location"]).query)["scope"] == [scope]


def test_a_signed_out_browser_is_sent_to_sign_in_and_back(client, db_session):
    _catalog(db_session, oauth_client_id="docs-client")

    resp = client.get(
        "/portal/connect/docs",
        params={"return_to": "http://localhost:3000/mcp"},
        follow_redirects=False,
    )

    location = urlsplit(resp.headers["location"])
    assert resp.status_code == 302
    assert location.path == "/auth/oauth/login"
    assert parse_qs(location.query)["next"] == [
        "/portal/connect/docs?return_to=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Fmcp"
    ]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "return_to, kept",
    [
        ("http://localhost:3000/mcp", True),
        ("https://attacker.example/", False),
        ("//attacker.example/", False),
        ("javascript:x", False),
    ],
)
def test_connecting_returns_only_to_an_allowed_origin(
    client, db_session, regular_user, discovered, monkeypatch, return_to, kept
):
    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS", "http://localhost:3000")
    _catalog(db_session, oauth_client_id="docs-client")
    _sign_in(client, regular_user.id)

    resp = client.get(
        "/portal/connect/docs", params={"return_to": return_to}, follow_redirects=True
    )

    state = jwt.decode(
        resp.history[-1].cookies[mcp_oauth.state_cookie()],
        settings.JWT_SECRET_KEY,
        algorithms=[settings.JWT_ALGORITHM],
    )
    assert json.loads(state["sub"])["return_to"] == (return_to if kept else None)


def test_each_server_has_its_own_redirect_uri(
    client, db_session, regular_user, discovered, register
):
    """So that its authorization server accepts no other server's address."""
    _catalog(db_session)
    _sign_in(client, regular_user.id)

    resp = client.get("/portal/connect-mcp-oauth/docs", follow_redirects=False)

    expected = f"{settings.GATEWAY_BASE_URL}/portal/callback/mcp-oauth/docs"
    query = parse_qs(urlsplit(resp.headers["location"]).query)
    assert query["redirect_uri"] == [expected]
    assert register.await_args.args[1] == expected


def test_a_failed_client_registration_does_not_show_the_servers_urls(
    client, db_session, admin_user, monkeypatch
):
    """Registration errors name the sign-in service's URLs, which are for admins."""
    _catalog(db_session, mcp_url="https://docs.internal.example/mcp")
    _sign_in(client, admin_user.id)
    metadata = MagicMock(registration_endpoint="https://auth.internal.example/reg")
    failure = RuntimeError(
        "Client error '400' for url 'https://auth.internal.example/reg'"
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        mcp_oauth, "resolve_oauth_metadata", AsyncMock(return_value=metadata)
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        mcp_oauth, "register_oauth_client", AsyncMock(side_effect=failure)
    )

    resp = client.get("/portal/connect-mcp-oauth/docs", follow_redirects=False)

    assert resp.status_code == 502
    assert "internal.example" not in resp.text


# --- the server's client id -----------------------------------------------------------


async def test_a_configured_client_id_is_used_as_is(db_session, dcr_metadata, register):
    mcp = _catalog(db_session, oauth_client_id="preconfigured-cid")

    client_id = await _resolve_client_id(mcp, dcr_metadata, REDIRECT_URI, db_session)

    assert client_id == "preconfigured-cid"
    register.assert_not_awaited()


async def test_a_client_is_registered_once_and_kept(db_session, dcr_metadata, register):
    mcp = _catalog(db_session)

    client_id = await _resolve_client_id(mcp, dcr_metadata, REDIRECT_URI, db_session)

    assert client_id == "dcr-issued-cid"
    register.assert_awaited_once_with(dcr_metadata.registration_endpoint, REDIRECT_URI)
    db_session.refresh(mcp)
    assert mcp.oauth_client_id == "dcr-issued-cid"


async def test_a_client_another_connect_just_registered_is_reused(
    db_engine, db_session, dcr_metadata, register
):
    """Two people connecting at once must not register two clients."""
    mcp = _catalog(db_session)
    with sessionmaker(bind=db_engine)() as other_connect:
        other_connect.query(MCPCatalog).filter(MCPCatalog.id == mcp.id).update(
            {"oauth_client_id": "registered-first"}
        )
        other_connect.commit()

    client_id = await _resolve_client_id(mcp, dcr_metadata, REDIRECT_URI, db_session)

    assert client_id == "registered-first"
    register.assert_not_awaited()


async def test_a_registered_client_id_that_is_the_gateways_is_refused(
    db_session, dcr_metadata, register
):
    """The gateway's own tokens go to servers whose client ID is the gateway's."""
    mcp = _catalog(db_session)
    register.return_value = settings.GATEWAY_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="gateway's client ID"):

    branches: [main, "branch-*"]

permissions:
  contents: read

  # A pull request keeps only its latest run. Each push to main or a release

  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

  UV_VERSION: "0.12.14"

  license:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check license headers

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Install uv
        run: python -m pip install "uv==${UV_VERSION}"
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --locked --all-extras
      - name: Check formatting

        run: |

          uv tool run --from "${BLACK}" black --check ${SOURCES}
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          uv tool run --from "${ISORT}" isort --check-only ${SOURCES}
      - name: Pylint
        run: |
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          uv run pylint ${SOURCES}
      - name: Unit tests
        run: uv run pytest -m "not integration"

  integration:
    name: Integration tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7

          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Install uv

          MCP_GATEWAY_KEYCLOAK_TEST: "1"
        run: uv run pytest -m integration tests/integration
      - name: Show service logs

      - name: Stop the services

"""Headers every response carries, unless the route set its own.

The gateway's pages and API responses hold tokens, codes and people's access,
so nothing is cached or framed by other sites, and pages send no referrer.
"""

from starlette.datastructures import MutableHeaders
from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send

DEFAULT_HEADERS = {
    "Cache-Control": "no-store",
    "Content-Security-Policy": "frame-ancestors 'none'",
    "Referrer-Policy": "no-referrer",
    "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
    "X-Frame-Options": "DENY",
}


class SecurityHeadersMiddleware:  # pylint: disable=too-few-public-methods
    """Adds DEFAULT_HEADERS to every HTTP response.

    A plain ASGI middleware, so streamed tool calls pass through untouched.
    """

    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, extra_headers: dict | None = None):
        self.app = app
        self.headers = {**DEFAULT_HEADERS, **(extra_headers or {})}

    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
            return

        async def send_with_headers(message: Message) -> None:
            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
                headers = MutableHeaders(scope=message)
                for name, value in self.headers.items():
                    if name not in headers:
                        headers[name] = value
            await send(message)

        await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_headers)

"""
OAuth Device Flow for CLI Authentication
"""

import json
import os
import webbrowser
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, Optional
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

import requests

from .constants import CONFIG_DIR, DEFAULT_GATEWAY_URL, TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN_SECONDS
from .device_flow import PollStatus, poll_device_token_until_done, request_device_code

TOKEN_FILE = CONFIG_DIR / "tokens"


class GatewayUnreachable(Exception):
    """The gateway didn't answer, or answered that it isn't working right now."""

    def __init__(self, gateway_url: str, reason: Optional[str] = None):
        super().__init__(
            f"{gateway_url} isn't working right now ({reason}). Try again shortly."
            if reason
            else f"Cannot reach {gateway_url}. "
            "Check the URL and that your network can reach it."
        )


def is_unreachable(error: Exception) -> bool:
    """Whether a request failed because nothing answered, rather than, say,
    because of a certificate that isn't trusted."""
    return isinstance(error, requests.ConnectionError) and not isinstance(
        error, requests.exceptions.SSLError
    )


def save_tokens(
    access_token: str,
    refresh_token: str,
    gateway_url: str,
    expires_in: int = 3600,
):
    """Save OAuth tokens and the gateway URL to file"""
    data = {
        "access_token": [REDACTED],
        "refresh_token": [REDACTED],
        "gateway_url": gateway_url,
        "expires_in": expires_in,
        "created_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
    }

    write_private_file(TOKEN_FILE, json.dumps(data, indent=2))


def write_private_file(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    """Replace ``path`` with ``text``, readable only by this user.

    The CLI and the proxy both write the token file, so it is replaced whole,
    and a reader never sees half of it.
    """
    path.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # mkdir's mode applies only to a directory it creates.
    path.parent.chmod(0o700)
    temporary = path.with_name(f".{path.name}.{os.getpid()}.tmp")
    descriptor = os.open(temporary, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
    with os.fdopen(descriptor, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(text)
    os.replace(temporary, path)


def load_tokens() -> Optional[Dict]:
    """Load OAuth tokens from file"""
    if not TOKEN_FILE.exists():
        return None

    try:
        with open(TOKEN_FILE, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
        return None


def get_gateway_url() -> str:
    """Get gateway URL from environment, saved tokens, or the local default"""
    # 1. Check environment variable
    env_url = os.getenv("MCP_GATEWAY_URL")
    if env_url:
        return env_url

    # 2. Check saved tokens
    tokens = load_tokens()
    if tokens and "gateway_url" in tokens:
        return tokens["gateway_url"]

    # 3. Default to a gateway on this machine
    return DEFAULT_GATEWAY_URL


def is_secure_gateway(gateway_url: str) -> bool:
    """Whether tokens may go to ``gateway_url``: over https, or to this machine."""
    parts = urlsplit(gateway_url)
    return parts.scheme == "https" or (
        parts.scheme == "http" and parts.hostname in ("localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1")
    )


def device_flow_login(gateway_url: str) -> bool:
    """
    Perform OAuth device flow login
    Returns True if successful, False otherwise
    """
    if not is_secure_gateway(gateway_url):
        print(
            f"The gateway must be an https URL, or one on this machine: {gateway_url}"
        )
        return False
    print(f"Authenticating with {gateway_url}...")

    # Step 1: Request device code
    try:
        device_data = request_device_code(gateway_url)
    except Exception as e:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
        print(
            GatewayUnreachable(gateway_url)
            if is_unreachable(e)
            else f"Failed to request device code: {e}"
        )
        return False

    verification_uri = device_data.verification_uri
    if not verification_uri.startswith(("https://", "http://")):
        print(f"The gateway sent an unexpected sign-in address: {verification_uri}")
        return False
    user_code = device_data.user_code
    expires_in = device_data.expires_in
    interval = device_data.interval

    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("Please complete the following steps:")
    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"\n1. Go to: {verification_uri}")
    print(f"2. Enter this code: {user_code}")
    print("\n" + "=" * 60)

    try:
        opened = webbrowser.open(verification_uri)
    except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
        opened = False
    print(
        "Browser opened automatically"
        if opened
        else "Open the URL above in a browser, on any device"
    )

    print(f"\nWaiting for approval (expires in {expires_in} seconds)...")

    result = poll_device_token_until_done(
        gateway_url,
        device_data.device_code,
        expires_in=expires_in,
        interval=interval,
        on_pending=lambda: print(".", end="", flush=True),
    )

    if result.status == PollStatus.SUCCESS and result.token_data:
        token_data = result.token_data
        save_tokens(
            token_data["access_token"],
            token_data.get("refresh_token", ""),
            gateway_url,
            token_data.get("expires_in", 3600),
        )
        print("\nSuccessfully authenticated!")
        print(f"Tokens saved to: {TOKEN_FILE}")
        print(f"Gateway: {gateway_url}")
        print("Tokens will auto-refresh before expiry")
        return True

    if result.status == PollStatus.EXPIRED:
        print("\nTimeout - device code expired")
        return False

    desc = result.error_description or result.error or "Unknown error"
    print(f"\nError: {desc}")
    return False


def get_access_token() -> Optional[str]:
    """A valid access token for the gateway the CLI talks to, refreshed if need be.

    None when the saved sign-in is for another gateway, such as when
    MCP_GATEWAY_URL names one: the token must not go anywhere but where it came from.
    """
    tokens = load_tokens()
    if not tokens:
        return None
    signed_in_at = tokens.get("gateway_url")
    if signed_in_at and signed_in_at != get_gateway_url():
        print(
            f"Your sign-in is for {signed_in_at}, not {get_gateway_url()}. "
            "Run 'gravitino-mcp login' to sign in there."
        )
        return None

    access_token = tokens.get("access_token")
    created_at = tokens.get("created_at")
    if not created_at:
        return access_token
    expires_in = tokens.get("expires_in", 3600)
    expires_at = datetime.fromisoformat(created_at) + timedelta(seconds=expires_in)
    if expires_at - datetime.utcnow() > timedelta(seconds=TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN_SECONDS):
        return access_token
    return _refreshed(access_token, expires_at)


def _refreshed(access_token: [REDACTED]], expires_at: datetime) -> Optional[str]:
    """A refreshed access token, or None once the sign-in has ended.

    While the gateway can't be reached, a token that hasn't expired is kept,
    since it works once the gateway answers; after that, GatewayUnreachable.
    """
    try:
        refreshed = refresh_access_token()
    except GatewayUnreachable:
        if expires_at > datetime.utcnow():
            return access_token
        raise
    if refreshed:
        tokens = load_tokens()
        return tokens.get("access_token") if tokens else None
    print(
        "Warning: Token refresh failed. Please run 'gravitino-mcp login' to re-authenticate."
    )
    return None


def refresh_access_token() -> bool:
    """
    Refresh the access token using refresh token via generic OIDC flow

    Uses gateway's refresh proxy endpoint to handle OIDC provider-specific details.
    This works with any OIDC provider (Azure AD, Okta, Auth0, Keycloak, etc.)
    """
    tokens = load_tokens()
    if not tokens or not tokens.get("refresh_token"):
        return False

    gateway_url = tokens.get("gateway_url")
    if not gateway_url:
        return False

    try:
        # Call gateway's generic refresh endpoint (provider-agnostic)
        response = requests.post(
            f"{gateway_url}/auth/refresh",
            json={"refresh_token": tokens["refresh_token"]},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {tokens['access_token']}"},
            timeout=10,
        )

        if response.status_code == 200:
            token_data = response.json()
            # Update stored tokens with refreshed values
            save_tokens(
                token_data["access_token"],
                token_data.get(
                    "refresh_token", tokens["refresh_token"]
                ),  # Keep old if not returned
                gateway_url,
                token_data.get("expires_in", 3600),
            )
            return True
        # A load balancer answers 502 or 503 while the gateway restarts.
        if response.status_code >= 500:
            raise GatewayUnreachable(gateway_url, f"HTTP {response.status_code}")
        print(
            f"Warning: Token refresh failed: {response.status_code} - {response.text}"
        )
        return False

    except GatewayUnreachable:
        raise
    except Exception as e:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
        if is_unreachable(e):
            raise GatewayUnreachable(gateway_url) from e
        # Only the gateway refusing the refresh token ends the sign-in.
        if isinstance(e, requests.RequestException) and not isinstance(
            e, requests.exceptions.SSLError
        ):
            reason = (
                "timed out" if isinstance(e, requests.Timeout) else "incomplete answer"
            )
            raise GatewayUnreachable(gateway_url, reason) from e
        print(f"Warning: Token refresh error: {e}")
        return False


def logout():
    """Remove stored tokens"""
    if TOKEN_FILE.exists():
        TOKEN_FILE.unlink()
        print("Logged out successfully")
    else:
        print("Not currently logged in")

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# https://oidc.eks.<region>.amazonaws.com/id/<cluster ID>, or .com.cn in China.
_EKS_ISSUER = re.compile(
    r"^https://oidc\.eks\.[a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com(?:\.cn)?/id/([0-9A-Za-z]+)/?$"
)
# How far apart the identity provider's clock and the gateway's may be.
JWT_LEEWAY_SECONDS = 60
# Google service accounts' emails.
_WORKLOAD_EMAIL_DOMAIN = ".gserviceaccount.com"
# https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0
_ENTRA_ISSUER = re.compile(r"^https://login\.microsoftonline\.com/([^/]+)/v2\.0/?$")

# One PyJWKClient per key endpoint, so its cached key set is shared. The set is
# fetched again after 5 minutes, and at most every 30 seconds for an unknown
# key ID. Keys aren't cached apart from the set: such a cache never expires,
# so a key the provider withdrew would stay trusted.
_jwks_clients: dict[str, PyJWKClient] = {}
_jwks_clients_lock = threading.Lock()

_JWKS_FETCH_MAX_RETRIES = 2
_JWKS_FETCH_RETRY_DELAY = 0.5  # seconds


def _get_jwks_client(jwks_uri: str) -> PyJWKClient:
    """Return a cached PyJWKClient for the given JWKS URI."""
    client = _jwks_clients.get(jwks_uri)
    if client is not None:
        return client
    with _jwks_clients_lock:
        # Double-check after acquiring lock
        client = _jwks_clients.get(jwks_uri)
        if client is None:
            client = PyJWKClient(
                jwks_uri,
                cache_keys=False,
                lifespan=300,
                timeout=settings.OIDC_HTTP_TIMEOUT,  # bound the blocking JWKS fetch
            )
            _jwks_clients[jwks_uri] = client
        return client


def _get_signing_key_with_retry(jwks_client: PyJWKClient, token: str):
    """Fetch the signing key, retrying on transient connection errors."""
    last_exc = None
    for attempt in range(_JWKS_FETCH_MAX_RETRIES + 1):
        try:
            return jwks_client.get_signing_key_from_jwt(token)
        except PyJWKClientConnectionError as exc:
            last_exc = exc
            if attempt < _JWKS_FETCH_MAX_RETRIES:
                logger.warning(
                    "JWKS fetch failed (attempt %d/%d), retrying: %s",
                    attempt + 1,
                    _JWKS_FETCH_MAX_RETRIES + 1,
                    exc,
                )
                time.sleep(_JWKS_FETCH_RETRY_DELAY * (attempt + 1))
    raise last_exc


def _service_account_trusted_issuers(
    sa_cred: ServiceAccountCredentials,
) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Issuers accepted for this service account before JWKS fetch or discovery."""
    if sa_cred.additional_config:
        pinned_iss = sa_cred.additional_config.get("iss")
        if isinstance(pinned_iss, str) and pinned_iss.strip():
            return frozenset({pinned_iss.strip()})
    return settings.trusted_issuer_set()


def _resolve_service_account_trusted_issuer(
    token_iss: str, sa_cred: ServiceAccountCredentials
) -> Optional[str]:
    """Return token_iss when it matches configured or registration-pinned issuers."""
    if not token_iss or not isinstance(token_iss, str):
        return None
    trusted = _service_account_trusted_issuers(sa_cred)
    if token_iss not in trusted:
        return None
    return token_iss


def _require_service_account_workload_headers(
    request: Request,
) -> None:
    """Reject a service-account request without a SERVICE_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED_HEADERS header."""
    for header in settings.service_account_required_headers:
        # Blank values aren't forwarded, so they don't count.
        if not (request.headers.get(header) or "").strip():
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=401,
                detail=f"{header} header is required for service account authentication.",
            )


def get_workload_forward_headers(request: Request) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return SA workload headers to forward to downstream MCP backends.

    Only service-account requests forward the configured workload headers.
    Human requests return an empty dict, so callers can do unconditional
    ``**get_workload_forward_headers(request)`` without forwarding (or auditing)
    workload attribution spoofed from arbitrary human-supplied headers.
    """
    if not getattr(request.state, "is_service_account", False):
        return {}
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for key in (
        settings.service_account_required_headers
        + settings.service_account_optional_headers
    ):
        v = request.headers.get(key)
        if v and v.strip():
            out[key] = v.strip()
    return out


def get_passthrough_forward_headers(request: Request) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return the caller's MCP_FORWARD_HEADERS headers to forward to the upstream MCP.

    Only the configured headers are forwarded, so arbitrary client headers
    can't be smuggled to backends. Additive to, and never overriding, the
    OAuth/auth headers MCP Gateway sets for the backend request.
    """
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for name in settings.mcp_forward_headers:
        v = request.headers.get(name)
        if v and v.strip():
            out[name] = v.strip()
    return out


def email_from_claims(claims: dict) -> Optional[str]:
    """A person's email from ID or access token claims, or None.

    Only a verified email claim identifies someone. Some providers, Keycloak
    among them, let people change their own email, which then reads
    unverified; a provider that leaves email_verified out may not check at all.
    Microsoft Entra ID's tokens carry no email_verified, and often no email,
    so there the email, UPN and username the tenant assigns stand in;
    elsewhere those claims can hold a name the person picked, such as an
    admin's email.
    """
    email = claims.get("email")  # Standard OIDC
    if email:
        verified = claims.get("email_verified")
        if verified is None and settings.OIDC_PROVIDER == "azure":
            return email
        if _is_true(verified):
            return email
        if verified is None:
            logger.warning(
                "A token for %s has no email_verified claim; the gateway trusts "
                "only verified emails, so add it to the provider's tokens",
                email,
            )
        return None
    if settings.OIDC_PROVIDER != "azure":
        return None
    return (
        claims.get("preferred_username")  # Azure AD
        or claims.get("upn")  # Azure AD (UPN)
        or claims.get("unique_name")  # Azure AD (legacy)
    )


async def sync_person(
    db: Session, claims: dict, email: str, token: [REDACTED]] = None
) -> Optional[User]:
    """Find or create the person ``email`` names, and update their name and admin flag.

    People are found by their verified email. Their username comes from
    USER_ID_CLAIM, so the gateway can name people the way Gravitino does.
    Admins are the people in ADMIN_EMAILS and, with GRAVITINO_URI set,
    Gravitino's service admins, checked with ``token``. Returns None for an
    email that a service account is registered under, or a deactivated account.
    """
    try:
        return await _sync_person(db, claims, email, token)
    except IntegrityError:
        # A concurrent sign-in created this person or took the name; start again.
        db.rollback()
        return await _sync_person(db, claims, email, token)


async def _sync_person(
    db: Session, claims: dict, email: str, token: [REDACTED]]
) -> Optional[User]:
    user = db.query(User).filter(User.email == email).first()
    if user is not None and user.email != email:
        # MySQL's collation finds an email that differs in case or accents;
        # creating the person then fails on the unique email, so no one signs in.
        user = None
    if user is not None and user.is_service_account:
        # A person must not take over a service account's row, name or rights.
        logger.warning("Refused a sign-in as %s, a service account", email)
        return None
    if user is not None and not user.is_active:
        return None
    username = _username_for(db, claims, email, user)
    if user is None:
        user = User(
            username=username,
            email=email,
            full_name=claims.get("name")
            or claims.get("given_name")
            or email.split("@")[0],
            is_admin=email in settings.admin_emails,
            is_service_account=False,
            is_active=True,
        )
        db.add(user)
        db.commit()
        db.refresh(user)
        logger.info("Created user %s", email)

    is_admin = email in settings.admin_emails or await is_gravitino_service_admin(
        db, user, token
    )
    if user.username == username and user.is_admin == is_admin:
        return user
    if user.is_admin != is_admin:
        logger.info("Set is_admin=%s for %s", is_admin, email)
    user.username = username
    user.is_admin = is_admin
    db.commit()
    return user


def _username_for(db: Session, claims: dict, email: str, user: Optional[User]) -> str:
    """The person's username: the USER_ID_CLAIM value, unique among accounts.

    A token without the claim keeps the current name, since ID tokens and
    access tokens can carry different claims. A name another account holds
    falls back to the email, and then to the email with a number.
    """
    claimed = claims.get(settings.USER_ID_CLAIM)
    if isinstance(claimed, str) and claimed.strip():
        # Other claims keep their case, as Gravitino reads them.
        wanted = claimed.strip()
        if settings.USER_ID_CLAIM == "email":
            wanted = wanted.lower()
    elif user is not None:
        return user.username
    else:
        wanted = email
    if not _username_taken(db, wanted, email):
        return wanted
    candidate, number = email, 2
    while _username_taken(db, candidate, email):
        candidate, number = f"{email}#{number}", number + 1
    if user is None or user.username != candidate:
        logger.warning(
            "%s %r of %s belongs to another account; naming them %r",
            settings.USER_ID_CLAIM,
            wanted,
            email,
            candidate,
        )
    return candidate


def _username_taken(db: Session, username: str, email: str) -> bool:
    """Whether an account other than ``email``'s has ``username``."""
    return (
        db.query(User.id).filter(User.username == username, User.email != email).first()
        is not None
    )


async def get_user_from_bearer_token(
    authorization: [REDACTED]] = Header(None, alias="Authorization"),
    request: Request = None,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> User:
    """
    The caller a bearer token names: a person, with a token from the gateway's
    identity provider, or a registered service account, with its workload
    identity token and the headers in SERVICE_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED_HEADERS.
    """
    if not authorization:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Authorization header required")

    if not authorization.startswith("Bearer "):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=401,
            detail="Invalid authorization header format. Use: Bearer <token>",
        )

    token = [REDACTED]"Bearer ", "").strip()

    if not token:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Token is empty")

    # Validate OIDC JWT (handles both human users and service accounts)
    if token.startswith("ey"):  # JWT tokens start with "ey"
        user = await _validate_oidc_jwt(token, db, request)
        if user:
            return user

    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=401,
        detail="Invalid or expired token. Please run: gravitino-mcp login",
    )


async def require_admin(user: User = Depends(get_user_from_bearer_token)) -> User:
    """The caller of an admin endpoint, who must be a gateway admin.

    Like the rest of the API, admin endpoints take only bearer tokens; the
    session cookie is for the gateway's own pages.
    """
    if not user.is_admin:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Admin privileges required")
    return user


def _extract_eks_iss_id(issuer: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """The cluster ID of an Amazon EKS OIDC issuer, in lower case, or None."""
    match = _EKS_ISSUER.match(issuer or "")
    return match.group(1).lower() if match else None


def _aws_service_account_identities(
    namespace: str, sa_name: str, issuer: str
) -> list[str]:
    """Candidate service_account_name values, most specific first."""
    legacy = f"{namespace}::{sa_name}"
    iss_id = _extract_eks_iss_id(issuer)
    if iss_id:
        return [f"{namespace}::{sa_name}::{iss_id}", legacy]
    return [legacy]


def _lookup_aws_service_account(
    db: Session, identities: list[str]
) -> Optional[ServiceAccountCredentials]:
    """The registration of the first identity that has one, or None.

    Every cluster has the same namespaces, so a ``namespace::name``
    registration counts only with ``additional_config.iss`` pinning one."""
    for identity in identities:
        identity_norm = identity.strip().lower()
        sa_cred = (
            db.query(ServiceAccountCredentials)
            .filter(
                func.lower(ServiceAccountCredentials.service_account_name)
                == identity_norm
            )
            .first()
        )
        if not sa_cred:
            continue
        pinned = (sa_cred.additional_config or {}).get("iss")
        if identity.count("::") == 1 and not (
            isinstance(pinned, str) and pinned.strip()
        ):
            logger.warning(
                "Service account %s names no cluster and pins no issuer", identity
            )
            return None
        return sa_cred
    return None


def _is_registered_service_account(db: Session, email_claim) -> bool:
    """Whether a token's email claim names a registered service account."""
    if not isinstance(email_claim, str) or not email_claim.strip():
        return False
    return (
        db.query(ServiceAccountCredentials.id)
        .filter(
            func.lower(ServiceAccountCredentials.service_account_name)
            == email_claim.strip().lower()
        )
        .first()
        is not None
    )


async def _is_human_token(
    db: Session, client_id: str, issuer: str, unverified_claims: dict
) -> bool:
    """Whether a token takes the human path rather than the service-account path."""
    if client_id in settings.gateway_oauth_client_ids:
        return True
    if not settings.GATEWAY_OAUTH_ACCEPT_ANY_CLIENT:
        return False
    if issuer != await run_in_threadpool(get_configured_issuer):
        return False
    # Workload identities can come from the same provider (for example Google),
    # so a registered service account keeps the service-account path.
    return not _is_registered_service_account(db, unverified_claims.get("email"))


async def _validate_oidc_jwt(
    token: str, db: Session, request: Request
) -> Optional[User]:
    """The person or service account a token names, or None if it names no one.

    The claims are read unverified only to choose a path; each path verifies the
    token's signature, issuer, audience and expiry before it trusts any claim.
    Every refusal looks the same to the caller, so tokens can't be used to find
    out which service accounts are registered.
    """
    triage = _triage(token)
    if triage is None:
        return None
    claims, issuer, cluster_id, client_id = triage
    try:
        if await _is_human_token(db, client_id, issuer, claims):
            return await _validate_human_user_jwt(token, issuer, db, request)
        return await _validate_service_account_jwt(
            token, claims, issuer, cluster_id, db, request
        )
    except HTTPException:
        raise
    except jwt.PyJWTError as e:
        # Including keys the issuer doesn't publish: anyone can send such a token.
        logger.info("Refused a token: %s", e)
        return None
    except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
        logger.exception("Error validating a token")
        return None


def _triage(token: str) -> Optional[tuple]:
    """A token's unverified claims, issuer, EKS cluster ID and client, or None."""
    try:
        claims = jwt.decode(token, options={"verify_signature": False})
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError:
        return None
    issuer = claims.get("iss")
    if not isinstance(issuer, str) or not issuer:
        return None
    cluster_id = _extract_eks_iss_id(issuer)
    # EKS tokens name the workload in sub; other providers name the client.
    client_id = (
        claims.get("sub")
        if cluster_id
        else (
            claims.get("appid")  # Entra ID
            or claims.get("azp")
            or claims.get("client_id")
            or claims.get("cid")  # Okta
        )
    )
    if not client_id:
        return None
    return claims, issuer, cluster_id, client_id


async def _validate_service_account_jwt(  # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments
    token: str,
    claims: dict,
    issuer: str,
    cluster_id: Optional[str],
    db: Session,
    request: Request,
) -> Optional[User]:
    """The registered service account a workload identity token names, or None."""
    sa_cred = _service_account_registration(db, claims, cluster_id)
    if sa_cred is None or not _resolve_service_account_trusted_issuer(issuer, sa_cred):
        return None
    jwks_uri = await _service_account_jwks_uri(sa_cred, issuer)
    if not jwks_uri:
        logger.error("Could not find the signing keys of issuer %s", issuer)
        return None
    decoded = await _verified_claims(
        token,
        jwks_uri,
        algorithms=["RS256", "RS384", "RS512"],
        issuer=issuer,
        audience=settings.service_account_audiences,
    )
    # A registration matches the email, which must be one the issuer checked.
    if cluster_id is None and not _is_true(decoded.get("email_verified")):
        return None

    service_account = (
        db.query(User)
        .filter(User.id == sa_cred.service_account_id, User.is_active.is_(True))
        .first()
    )
    if service_account is None or request is None:
        return None

    _require_service_account_workload_headers(request)
    # Its workload headers are forwarded to MCP servers and written to the audit log.
    request.state.is_service_account = True
    logger.info("Service account %s authenticated", service_account.username)
    return service_account


def _service_account_registration(
    db: Session, claims: dict, cluster_id: Optional[str]
) -> Optional[ServiceAccountCredentials]:
    """The registration that an unverified token's identity claims name, or None.

    GCP tokens name the service account's email; EKS tokens name the
    Kubernetes service account and, in the issuer, the cluster.
    """
    email = claims.get("email")
    if isinstance(email, str) and email.strip():
        return (
            db.query(ServiceAccountCredentials)
            .filter(
                func.lower(ServiceAccountCredentials.service_account_name)
                == email.strip().lower()
            )
            .first()
        )
    kubernetes = claims.get("kubernetes.io")
    if cluster_id is None or not isinstance(kubernetes, dict):
        return None
    account = kubernetes.get("serviceaccount")
    namespace = kubernetes.get("namespace")
    name = account.get("name") if isinstance(account, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(namespace, str) or not isinstance(name, str):
        return None
    return _lookup_aws_service_account(
        db, _aws_service_account_identities(namespace, name, claims["iss"])
    )


async def _service_account_jwks_uri(
    sa_cred: ServiceAccountCredentials, issuer: str
) -> Optional[str]:
    """Where the signing keys of a service account's issuer are."""
    pinned = (sa_cred.additional_config or {}).get("jwks_uri")
    if pinned:
        return pinned
    return settings.trusted_issuer_jwks_map().get(issuer) or await _discover_jwks_uri(
        issuer, allowed_issuers=_service_account_trusted_issuers(sa_cred)
    )


async def _verified_claims(
    token: str, jwks_uri: str, *, algorithms: list, issuer: str, audience
) -> dict:
    """The claims of ``token`` once its signature, issuer, audience and expiry check out."""
    # The key fetch is synchronous, so it runs in a worker thread.
    signing_key = await run_in_threadpool(
        _get_signing_key_with_retry, _get_jwks_client(jwks_uri), token
    )
    return jwt.decode(
        token,
        signing_key.key,
        algorithms=algorithms,
        issuer=issuer,
        audience=audience,
        # Without an expiry a stolen token would work for ever.
        options={"require": ["exp"]},
        # The provider's clock and the gateway's may differ by a little.
        leeway=JWT_LEEWAY_SECONDS,
    )


def _is_true(value) -> bool:
    return value is True or str(value).lower() == "true"


# Each issuer's JWKS URI, from its discovery document: issuer -> (uri, when).
_jwks_uri_cache: dict[str, tuple[str, float]] = {}


def _eks_oidc_jwks_uri(issuer: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Return the public JWKS URL for an Amazon EKS cluster OIDC issuer."""
    if _extract_eks_iss_id(issuer) is None:
        return None
    return f"{issuer.rstrip('/')}/keys"


async def _discover_jwks_uri(  # pylint: disable=too-many-locals
    issuer: str, *, allowed_issuers: frozenset[str]
) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Discover JWKS URI from an already-trusted issuer's discovery document.

    ``issuer`` must be present in ``allowed_issuers``; untrusted issuers are
    rejected without making a network request.
    """
    if issuer not in allowed_issuers:
        logger.warning("Refusing JWKS discovery for untrusted issuer: %s", issuer)
        return None

    now = time.monotonic()

    cached = _jwks_uri_cache.get(issuer)
    if cached:
        uri, ts = cached
        if now - ts < settings.OIDC_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL:
            return uri

    discovery_urls = [
        f"{issuer.rstrip('/')}/.well-known/openid-configuration",
        f"{issuer.rstrip('/')}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server",
    ]

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=settings.OIDC_HTTP_TIMEOUT) as client:
        for url in discovery_urls:
            try:
                response = await client.get(url)
                if response.status_code == 200:
                    config = response.json()
                    jwks_uri = config.get("jwks_uri")
                    if jwks_uri:
                        logger.info("Discovered JWKS URI from %s: %s", url, jwks_uri)
                        _jwks_uri_cache[issuer] = (jwks_uri, now)
                        return jwks_uri
            except Exception as e:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
                logger.debug("Failed to fetch discovery from %s: %s", url, e)
                continue

    # Entra ID and EKS publish their keys at known places.
    known = _ENTRA_ISSUER.match(issuer)
    jwks_uri = (
        f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{known.group(1)}/discovery/v2.0/keys"
        if known
        else _eks_oidc_jwks_uri(issuer)
    )
    if jwks_uri:
        logger.info("Using the known key endpoint of %s: %s", issuer, jwks_uri)
        _jwks_uri_cache[issuer] = (jwks_uri, now)
        return jwks_uri

    logger.warning("Could not discover JWKS URI for issuer: %s", issuer)
    return None


async def _validate_human_user_jwt(
    token: str,
    issuer: str,
    db: Session,
    request: Request,
) -> Optional[User]:
    """The person a token from the gateway's identity provider names, or None."""
    # The issuer may come from the discovery document, whose first fetch
    # blocks, so it is resolved in a worker thread.
    configured_issuer = await run_in_threadpool(get_configured_issuer)
    if not configured_issuer:
        logger.error("Signing people in needs OIDC_ISSUER or OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL")
        return None
    if issuer != configured_issuer:
        return None

    jwks_uri = (settings.OIDC_JWKS_URI or "").strip() or await _discover_jwks_uri(
        configured_issuer, allowed_issuers=frozenset({configured_issuer})
    )
    if not jwks_uri:
        logger.error("Could not find the signing keys of issuer %s", configured_issuer)
        return None
    decoded = await _verified_claims(
        token,
        jwks_uri,
        algorithms=["RS256"],
        issuer=configured_issuer,
        audience=settings.JWT_AUDIENCE,
    )

    email = _person_email(decoded)
    user = await sync_person(db, decoded, email, token) if email else None
    if user is None:
        return None

    if request:
        request.state.bearer_token = token  # For token exchange.
    logger.debug("%s authenticated", user.email)
    return user


def _person_email(claims: dict) -> Optional[str]:
    """The email, in lower case, of the person verified claims name, or None."""
    email = email_from_claims(claims)
    if not email:
        logger.warning(
            "A token has no verified email or account name (tried: email, "
            "preferred_username, upn, unique_name)"
        )
        return None
    if email.lower().endswith(_WORKLOAD_EMAIL_DOMAIN):
        # Any Google service account can get a token for any audience, so one
        # that isn't registered must not become a person.
        logger.warning("Refused a person's sign-in as the workload %s", email)
        return None
    return email.lower()

"""
Downstream MCP auth helpers: effective auth strategy and credential forwarding.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import logging
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from ..config import settings
from ..models import MCPCatalog, ServiceAccountCredentials, User
from .secret_storage import get_secret_storage
from .token_encryption import SECRET_NAME as ENCRYPTION_KEY_SECRET

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Keys in ``ServiceAccountCredentials.additional_config`` JSON (per MCP service id).
DOWNSTREAM_CREDENTIALS = "downstream_credentials"
SECRET_REF = "secret_ref"
AUTH_HEADER_TYPE = "auth_header_type"
USERNAME = "username"

AUTH_HEADER_BASIC = "basic"
AUTH_HEADER_BEARER = "bearer"
_VALID_AUTH_HEADER_TYPES = frozenset({AUTH_HEADER_BASIC, AUTH_HEADER_BEARER})


def secret_ref_allowed(secret_ref: str) -> bool:
    """Whether a service account may forward the secret named ``secret_ref``.

    The gateway's identity can read secrets other than service accounts', such
    as its own encryption key or, in a shared cloud account, other services'.
    An admin must not be able to read those by naming them here.
    """
    return secret_ref != ENCRYPTION_KEY_SECRET and secret_ref.startswith(
        settings.SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SECRET_PREFIX
    )


def refused_secret_refs(additional_config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> list[str]:
    """The secret names in a service account's config that it may not forward."""
    forwarding = (additional_config or {}).get(DOWNSTREAM_CREDENTIALS)
    if not isinstance(forwarding, dict):
        return []
    refs = [cfg.get(SECRET_REF) for cfg in forwarding.values() if isinstance(cfg, dict)]
    return [
        ref
        for ref in refs
        if isinstance(ref, str) and ref.strip() and not secret_ref_allowed(ref.strip())
    ]


def effective_auth_type(mcp: MCPCatalog, user: User) -> str:
    """Pick downstream auth strategy.

    Service-account callers use ``mcp.service_auth_type`` when set; otherwise fall
    back to ``mcp.auth_type``. Human callers always use ``mcp.auth_type``.
    """
    service_auth_type = getattr(mcp, "service_auth_type", None)
    if user.is_service_account and service_auth_type and str(service_auth_type).strip():
        return str(service_auth_type).strip()
    return mcp.auth_type


async def build_credential_forward_headers(  # pylint: disable=too-many-return-statements
    db: Session, user: User, service: str
) -> Optional[Dict[str, str]]:
    """Resolve Authorization header from SA ``additional_config`` + ``DOWNSTREAM_CREDENTIALS``.

    ``SECRET_REF`` is passed to :meth:`SecretStorage.get_secret` — for GCP that is the
    short secret **id** inside ``GCP_PROJECT_ID`` (not a full ``projects/…`` resource path).
    """
    if not user.is_service_account:
        return None

    sa = (
        db.query(ServiceAccountCredentials)
        .filter(ServiceAccountCredentials.service_account_id == user.id)
        .first()
    )
    if not sa:
        return None

    cfg_any: Any = (
        (sa.additional_config or {}).get(DOWNSTREAM_CREDENTIALS, {}).get(service)
    )
    if not isinstance(cfg_any, dict):
        return None

    cfg: Dict[str, Any] = cfg_any

    secret_ref = cfg.get(SECRET_REF)
    if not secret_ref or not isinstance(secret_ref, str) or not secret_ref.strip():
        return None

    auth_raw = cfg.get(AUTH_HEADER_TYPE)
    if not auth_raw or not isinstance(auth_raw, str) or not auth_raw.strip():
        return None
    header_type = auth_raw.strip().lower()
    if header_type not in _VALID_AUTH_HEADER_TYPES:
        logger.warning(
            "credential_forward: invalid %s=%r for user_id=%s service=%s",
            AUTH_HEADER_TYPE,
            auth_raw,
            user.id,
            service,
        )
        return None

    if header_type == AUTH_HEADER_BASIC:
        username = cfg.get(USERNAME)
        if not username or not isinstance(username, str) or not username.strip():
            return None

    if not secret_ref_allowed(secret_ref.strip()):
        logger.warning(
            "credential_forward: refused secret %r for user_id=%s service=%s; "
            "names must start with SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SECRET_PREFIX",
            secret_ref[:64],
            user.id,
            service,
        )
        return None

    storage = get_secret_storage()
    credential = await storage.get_secret(secret_ref.strip())
    if not credential:
        logger.warning(
            "credential_forward: could not fetch secret for user_id=%s service=%s ref=%s",
            user.id,
            service,
            secret_ref[:64],
        )
        return None

    if header_type == AUTH_HEADER_BASIC:
        username = cfg[USERNAME].strip()
        encoded = base64.b64encode(f"{username}:{credential}".encode()).decode()
        return {"Authorization": f"Basic {encoded}"}
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {credential}"}

"""
Token Encryption Utility - Industry Standard Approach
Uses AES-256-GCM for encrypting OAuth tokens in database
The key comes from TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE or the secret storage.
"""

import base64
import binascii
import logging
import os
from typing import Optional

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM

from ..config import settings
from .secret_storage import get_secret_storage

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SECRET_NAME = "mcp-gateway-encryption-key"


class TokenEncryption:
    """
    Encrypts/decrypts OAuth tokens using AES-256-GCM

    Industry standard approach:
    - One master key in Secret Manager
    - Encrypted tokens in database
    - Fast, scalable, cost-effective
    """

    def __init__(self, encryption_key: bytes):
        """
        Initialize with 32-byte encryption key

        Args:
            encryption_key: 32-byte AES-256 key from Secret Manager
        """
        if len(encryption_key) != 32:
            raise ValueError("Encryption key must be 32 bytes for AES-256")

        self.aesgcm = AESGCM(encryption_key)

    def encrypt(self, plaintext: str) -> str:
        """
        Encrypt a token using AES-256-GCM

        Args:
            plaintext: Token to encrypt

        Returns:
            Base64-encoded encrypted token with nonce
        """
        # Generate random 12-byte nonce for GCM
        nonce = os.urandom(12)

        # Encrypt
        ciphertext = self.aesgcm.encrypt(nonce, plaintext.encode("utf-8"), None)

        # Combine nonce + ciphertext and base64 encode
        encrypted = nonce + ciphertext
        return base64.b64encode(encrypted).decode("utf-8")

    def decrypt(self, encrypted: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Decrypt a token using AES-256-GCM

        Args:
            encrypted: Base64-encoded encrypted token

        Returns:
            Decrypted token or None if decryption fails
        """
        try:
            # Decode from base64
            encrypted_bytes = base64.b64decode(encrypted)

            # Extract nonce (first 12 bytes) and ciphertext
            nonce = encrypted_bytes[:12]
            ciphertext = encrypted_bytes[12:]

            # Decrypt
            plaintext = self.aesgcm.decrypt(nonce, ciphertext, None)
            return plaintext.decode("utf-8")

        except Exception as e:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
            # Log error but don't expose details
            logger.error("Token decryption failed: %s", type(e).__name__)
            return None


# Global encryption instance (initialized on first use)
_token_encryption: Optional[TokenEncryption] = None  # pylint: disable=invalid-name


def _configured_key() -> Optional[str]:
    """The base64 key from TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY or TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE, if set."""
    if settings.TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY:
        return settings.TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY
    if settings.TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE:
        with open(settings.TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE, encoding="utf-8") as key_file:
            return key_file.read()
    return None


async def get_token_encryption() -> TokenEncryption:
    """
    Get or initialize the token encryption instance

    Lazy-loads the encryption key on first use

    Returns:
        TokenEncryption instance
    """
    global _token_encryption  # pylint: disable=global-statement

    if _token_encryption is None:
        encryption_key_b64 = _configured_key()
        if not encryption_key_b64:
            encryption_key_b64 = await get_secret_storage().get_secret(SECRET_NAME)

        if not encryption_key_b64:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Encryption key not found. Set TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY or "
                "TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE, or store a base64-encoded 32-byte key "
                f"in the secret storage as {SECRET_NAME}"
            )

        try:
            encryption_key = base64.b64decode(encryption_key_b64.strip())
        except binascii.Error as e:
            raise RuntimeError("The token encryption key is not valid base64") from e

        _token_encryption = TokenEncryption(encryption_key)

    return _token_encryption
